extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant reviewers, prospective PIs, and institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Describe institutional facilities, biosafety/compliance programs, cores, equipment, and IT/data management resources in support of an NIH grant application. Emphasizes available space, certified containment labs, core services, and policies required for safe, compliant research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory space allocation and proximity of offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of buildings (Moorman, Earl Slick, Urschel-Slick, Ledford) listing square footage of laboratories and offices and the number of faculty supported (e.g., Moorman: 12 labs, 9,459 sq. ft., supports 6-12 faculty; Earl Slick: 14 labs, 12,298 sq. ft., supports 7-14 faculty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities should provide adequate lab and adjacent office space for faculty, staff and trainees, with dedicated technician offices and proximity between labs and offices to support research operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated phlebotomy facilities and trained personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated blood draw room adjacent to BSL2 lab space equipped with refrigerator, phlebotomy chair (Trendelenburg capable), and privacy measures; only trained individuals serve as phlebotomists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical sample collection areas must ensure donor privacy and be staffed only by trained phlebotomists with appropriate equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to external institutional core facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: UT Health San Antonio cores available within ~10–15 minutes (Mass Spectrometry, Bioanalytics & Single cell, Biobanking & Genome Analysis, Biomolecular NMR, Flow Cytometry, Macromolecular interactions, Micro-CT, Electron Microscopy, Optical Imaging, X-ray Crystallography).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting nearby external cores demonstrates access to specialized assays and instrumentation not housed onsite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects oversight via IRB joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Human subject studies reviewed by UT Health San Antonio Institutional Review Board through a joinder agreement; UT Health affiliates specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical research must have IRB oversight; a joinder or affiliation should be documented when using external IRBs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care program compliance and accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Texas Biomed has an independent Institutional Animal Care and Use Program responsible for USDA and AAALAC standards and adheres to the Animal Welfare Act, PHS Policy, and the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals. Animal Welfare Assurance #A308201 and continuous AAALAC accreditation since 1973 (AAALAC File #000246).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal research facilities must document compliance with federal policies and accreditation status to support vertebrate animal work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated vivarium and veterinary support
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated rodent vivarium located in Slick-Urschel with current capacity on ventilated racks or static caging, expansion space, a dedicated supervisor and staff, and veterinary care; vivarium staff support rodent studies at ABSL3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Onsite vivarium capacity and professional support are required to conduct and expand animal studies safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onsite computing resources and connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: 57 desktop and 31 laptop computers plus printers/fax in Moorman and adjacent buildings and library; connected to central network and protected by UPS devices; 100 Mb/s Ethernet leased router.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient workstation availability and network capacity for instrument operation, data management, and analysis should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and programming environment availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to a wide variety of programming languages (FORTRAN, C, C++, Java, Tcl, Perl, Python, Ruby, bash, R) and statistical/mathematical packages (GraphPad, Maple, S-PLUS, R). Specific software/packages can be installed on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare available software environments and the ability to install required packages for proposed analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT support staff and ticket system
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated IT staff of 9 led by the VP for Information Technology maintains systems, assists scientists with installations and debugging; a ticket system is in place; expertise in SQL and in-house PEDSYS database management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe available IT personnel, helpdesk processes, and database expertise to support project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and system security measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Security measures compliant with IRB requirements: Palo Alto Networks next-generation security appliances in redundant configuration; SSH/SFTP and VPN connections; removal of network access upon employment termination; periodic checks of access logs and countermeasures on suspicious activity; access to central files restricted to approved user lists maintained per unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document network security architecture, access control policies, monitoring, and procedures for terminating access to protect research and human subject data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backup and long-term data archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: Disk-based daily incremental and monthly full backups using Veritas NetBackup; long-term archiving provided by multiple tape libraries (described configurations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide backup cadence, system used, and long-term archive capabilities to ensure data integrity and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: REDCap availability for data capture and management
rubrics_metrics.description: REDCap is available as a secure, web-based application for building/managing online surveys and databases with automated export to common statistical packages, project calendar, scheduling, reporting, branching logic, file upload, and calculated fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of REDCap (or equivalent) should be stated for secure clinical and research data collection and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSL4 laboratory certification and unique capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Texas Biomed houses the only operational private-institution ABSL4 lab that is CDC and USDA certified, supporting basic research and vaccine/therapeutics testing for agents with no cure (e.g., Ebola, Marburg).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document high-containment lab certifications and unique institutional capabilities that directly support the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSL4 physical access controls and decontamination features
rubrics_metrics.description: Access secured via three successive magnetic card/keypad controlled airlocks; entry/exit decontamination airlock; emergency exit/decontamination chamber; entry/outer/inner changer rooms and pass-through showers; outer 'clean' change room with sinks, lockers, toilets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-containment labs must describe layered access controls and decontamination infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSL4 air handling and redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: All supply and exhaust air passes through dual/tandem HEPA filters; critical mechanical devices and systems are redundant (duplicate air-supply/exhaust, decontamination showers, compressors, pumps, valves, heater cores); systems supported by automatic emergency electricity backup generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on air filtration, redundancy of critical systems, and emergency power to demonstrate containment reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous monitoring and personnel communications in ABSL4
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical parameters (air flows, pressure differentials, breathing air, decontamination systems) are continuously monitored; personnel communicate via scrambled UHF internal suit system and are actively monitored by outside personnel; intrusion detection (door/roof sensors, motion detectors) present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe real-time monitoring of environmental and security parameters and communication systems for personnel safety and containment oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSL4 instrumentation and laboratory equipment inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: List of core ABSL4 equipment (class IIB hoods, CO2 incubators, centrifuges, microfuge, refrigerators, liquid nitrogen systems, -80°C freezers, ELISA reader, MAGPIX, luminometer, environmental shaker, microscopes, pass-through autoclave, dunk tank, networked computers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an inventory of available high-containment laboratory equipment relevant to the proposed methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABSL4 operations manuals and SOP compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations and Safety Manuals specify policies, procedures, and SOPs for safe handling of biological materials in biosafety labs; policies comply with applicable Federal, State, municipal regulations and CDC/NIH BMBL guidance; employees trained from these manuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite institutional SOPs and alignment with national biosafety guidance and regulations to support safety compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infectious material storage and electronic inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Infectious cultures and stocks are stored in locked refrigerators/freezers; an electronic Inventory (eInventory) system documents usage; containers labeled with agent identity, date of preparation, and barcode linking to database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe inventory controls, secure storage, and labeling practices for infectious materials to ensure traceability and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and disposal procedures for infectious waste
rubrics_metrics.description: When work is completed, infectious cultures removed from benches and stored; materials to be discarded placed in sealable containers with disinfectant, placed in a discard pan, transported to autoclave; labware containing infectious liquids stored/transported in leak-proof containers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail decontamination, containment, and autoclaving workflows for safe disposal of infectious materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select agent use and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Use, transfer or possession of select agents forbidden without permission of the Responsible Official (RO) and until required forms filed and written approval from CDC Select Agent Program received; upon approval, investigators must also submit application to the Biohazard and Safety Committee for evaluation of facility, equipment, and staff capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document RO/ARO permissions, required regulatory filings, and institutional committee review for select agent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized Biocontainment Program and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution-wide centralized BSL3/BSL4 and CDC certified Select Agent BSL3 facilities program ensures coordinated development, technical support coordination, optimized training, and broad campus expertise; managed by BSL3 Director, BSL4 Director, two coordinators, and overseen by a Biosafety-3/4 Advisory Committee (BAC) with VP for Research/RO participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance structures and committees should be described to show coordinated oversight, rule development, and evaluation of facility use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) oversight and services
rubrics_metrics.description: EHS provides institutional BSL3/4 compliance oversight and services including radiation safety, environmental compliance, occupational health and safety, research safety and biosafety; program director, Responsible Official, alternate, and Biohazardous and Safety Committee exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State EHS roles and available compliance services that support regulated research activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSL3/4 user training and access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Access granted only after thorough biosafety and biosecurity training and proper on-site training; training materials reviewed by RO/ARO; refresher training annually; time-sensitive issues discussed monthly in user group (BUG); on-site training demonstrates PPE application and facility features; junior scientists must be accompanied and supervised by experienced senior scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline training curricula, review/approval of materials, refresher schedules, and supervision policies for trainees and new users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent registration and inspection status
rubrics_metrics.description: Texas Biomed is a select agent registered entity with HHS/CDC and USDA APHIS National Select Agent Program and has been inspected for HHS/USDA Select Agents and Toxins (registration number provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registration and inspection status to demonstrate regulatory compliance for select agent research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biology Core microscopy and image analysis capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Core operates Zeiss LSM800 and Nikon C2+ confocal microscopes, Nikon Ti Eclipse widefield with automated acquisition, ANDOR iXon3 EMCCD camera, AutoQuant X3, Imaris, CellProfiler, FCSExpress, ImageJ; objective and incubator stage details provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List imaging platforms, software, and analysis pipelines available for quantitative microscopy and high-content screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of advanced flow cytometry platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: BD FACSymphony 5-laser, 28-color with High Throughput Sampler (since Sept 2019) for high-sensitivity multiplex panels; Beckman Coulter Cyan ADP (11 parameters); BD Accuri C6 Plus (4-color, dedicated to BSL2+ HIV); BD FACSAria cell sorter (18-color, 4-way sorting) contained within high-containment cabinet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document capabilities of cytometers and sorters to support multiparameter immunophenotyping and sorting requirements of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular Services Core equipment and sequencing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Illumina iSeq 100 and MiSeq sequencers, automated liquid handler (Sciclone G3 NGSx), 10X Genomics Chromium, Fluidigm C1, Sage PippinHT, Agilent Bioanalyzer/TapeStation, Nanodrop, Qubit, multiple PCR machines, QuantStudio systems (including digital PCR), iScan with autoloader, Tecan automation, BioRad Chemidoc, ultracentrifuges, and a dedicated analysis server (Dell PowerEdge R830, 48 cores, 32TB usable, 256GB RAM) with Partek Flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide available NGS platforms, sample prep automation, real-time and digital PCR systems, analysis servers, and bioinformatics support to demonstrate end-to-end genomic capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathology and histology facility capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Necropsy, hematology, chemistry, tissue processing, slide processing, refrigeration, storage, and image capture spaces described; necropsy equipped with downdraft table, HEPA bone saw, perfusion fixation, Nikon D200 gross imaging; histology lab provides processing, embedding, sectioning, routine and special stains, IHC, automated stainers, cryostat, microtomes, imaging cameras; developed IHC procedures and list of available antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail pathology/histology workflows, instrumentation, imaging, and available IHC reagents relevant to tissue-based analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onsite major equipment for chemistry and computational chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Fox Chase Chemical Diversity Center equipment list: NMRs (Varian Mercury Plus 300 MHz), HPLC/MS (Micromass ZQ with Waters 2695), semi-prep HPLCs, automated chromatography systems, evaporation systems, rotavapors, hydrogenation units, microwave synthesizer, reactors, shakers, BL2 tissue culture equipment, microscopes, computational hardware (workstations, GPU server) and software (Schrodinger suite, GROMACS), SciFinder-n, and extensive reagents/starting materials collection (>30,000 items bar-coded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chemical synthesis, analytical, and computational resources that support medicinal chemistry and small molecule discovery activities.
